slot.subtopic: Perpendicular distance from point to line
slot.brief: find coordinates of the foot of the perpendicular from a point to a line in 3-space using vector projection

stem: The foot of the perpendicular from the point $(3,3,3)$ to the line $\dfrac{x-1}{2} = \dfrac{y-2}{3} = \dfrac{z-3}{6}$ is
solution: A point on the line is $A=(1,2,3)$, with direction vector $�d=(2,3,6)$. For $P=(3,3,3)$, the foot is $H=A+t�d$, where $t=\dfrac{(P-A)\cdot\u0000d}{|\u0000d|^2}=\dfrac{7}{49}=\dfrac17$. Thus $H=(1,2,3)+\dfrac17(2,3,6)=\left(\dfrac97,\dfrac{17}7,\dfrac{27}7\right)$.
